items.evidence: The opener claim itself holds: אַ֤תְּ (oshb:Song.6.4, byte tier) is the 2fs independent pronoun and רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.6.4, byte tier) the attested his-word address. But the surface audit of word-final-kaf 2fs forms across the span runs MT 6:5 = 2 (עֵינַ֨יִךְ֙, הִרְהִיבֻ֑נִי, oshb:Song.6.5), MT 6:6 = 1 (שִׁנַּ֨יִךְ֙, oshb:Song.6.6), MT 6:7 = 2 (רַקָּתֵ֔ךְ, לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ, oshb:Song.6.7), MT 6:8 = 0, MT 6:9 = 0; MT 6:9 instead predicates הִיא֙ (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) three times with the 3fs mappiq suffixes לְאִמָּ֔הּ and לְיֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) and three 3fs object suffixes; the 1cs epithets יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) there are possessive, not address forms. 'The same male address-voice governs the whole span' is therefore true of MT 6:4-6:7 only, and the rejected-alternative's reason for keeping the wider bound - that no tier-1 marker licenses the 6:7/6:8 cut - is contradicted by the row's own evidence class. items.evidence: The quoted run collates at byte tier against oshb:Song.6.10. MT 6:9 predicates אַחַ֥ת הִיא֙ (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) with הִיא֙ (oshb:Song.6.9) three times in the verse, the 3fs mappiq suffixes לְאִמָּ֔הּ / לְיֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) and three 3fs object suffixes; MT 6:10 continues feminine-singular predication with הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier). Conceding the row's best case: יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier) are 1cs-POSSESSIVE epithets, addressive in flavour but not address forms - the last actual 2fs address in the neighbourhood is לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ (oshb:Song.6.7, byte tier), three verses earlier. So 'bounded on both sides by a person-form shift' holds on the back side only (3fs to 1cs at MT 6:11). Tier defect on the recurrence: the row's own מִי זֹ֥את (oshb:Song.6.10) is byte tier at 1 verse; the three-site count is an accent-stripped/skeleton object (sweep: 3 verses at both those tiers - MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5 - the other two differently pointed), and no tier is named for it. The label imports a byte-absent element: מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier) shows the ascending verb attested at MT 3:6 and MT 8:5 and absent from MT 6:10, whose participle is הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier), so 'ascending-question' is not a description of this verse's bytes. Undisclosed byte-identical cross-seam device: אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier) closes this verse and closes MT 6:4 byte-identically (byte sweep: 2 verses), an inclusio straddling the row's front seam that argues MT 6:10 is the closing member of the preceding praise frame; בָּרָה֙ (oshb:Song.6.10) / בָּרָ֥ה הִ֖יא (oshb:Song.6.9) runs the same way. items.claim: The row states that every structured ref on it carries the dual-cite qualifier and that is false - its rejected-alternative sentence carries a bare offset-zone coordinate - and it argues its own held voice crux without quoting the verse's decisive plural form.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs collate at byte tier against oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, and the duals written in the rationale and in the evidence refs are arithmetically right through the crosswalk. Offset-zone disclosure fails in prose: the rejected-alternative field writes the structured coordinate 'web:Song.7.1' bare - no dual, no numeric qualifier - while the row's own note asserts that every structured ref on it is qualified. In this book that bare coordinate means oshb:Song.7.2, and standing in a sentence about extending the row FORWARD it is readable as the row's own verse (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13); the deterministic ref arm covers the evidence-ref list, so this one surfaces at rule level rather than as a machine flag. Engagement gap on the row's own crux: it holds open whether the second half's speaker matches the first, then quotes שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי and תֶּחֱזוּ֙ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) while omitting the form between them that decides the plural question - וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a 1cp cohortative with a 2fs suffix, i.e. the byte evidence that the summoners are plural and the addressee feminine, which is exactly what the 2mp form is being weighed against. Undisclosed cross-seam catchword: נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) immediately before and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier) immediately after bracket this single-verse span on both seams - skeleton sweep: 2 verses book-wide - and the interrogative particle opens both the second half of this verse, מַֽה (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13), and the following verse, מַה (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1) - skeleton tier only, the two are not byte-identical (meteg on the first), and this is the short-token class, cited with that caveat. Worth crediting and unclaimed: הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) occurs in this verse only, twice in-verse (byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide) - genuine support for holding the verse whole; no K/Q note falls in the offset zone and no parashah seg sits at either seam, both correctly left unclaimed.
